title: Forward-active region and the Early effect

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
In a real BJT the collector current rises slowly with \(V_{CE}\), even in forward-active. A higher collector-base reverse bias widens the collector depletion region, and part of that widening extends into the base. The neutral base gets thinner, the electron gradient gets steeper, and \(I_C\) increases. This is **base-width modulation**, the Early effect.

If you extend the forward-active curves backward, they meet near \(V_{CE} = -V_A\), where \(V_A\) is the Early voltage. The slope of each curve defines an output resistance \(r_o\). An ideal current source would have flat curves and infinite \(r_o\); the Early effect is what keeps a real transistor from being one. Typical integrated npn devices have \(V_A\) of tens of volts, which gives \(r_o\) of tens to hundreds of kilohms at ordinary bias currents, large but not negligible in high-gain stages.
sections.figure_alt: Collector curves in forward-active sloping upward; extended backward to negative V_CE they all meet the axis near V_CE = -V_A, the Early voltage.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ I_C = I_Se^{V_{BE}/V_{th}}\left(1 + \frac{V_{CE}}{V_A}\right) \]
\[ r_o = \left(\frac{\partial I_C}{\partial V_{CE}}\right)^{-1} \approx \frac{V_A}{I_C} \]
\(V_A\) plays the same role for the BJT that \(1/\lambda\) plays for a MOSFET.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md:
A device with \(V_A = 75\ \mathrm{V}\) at \(I_C = 0.25\ \mathrm{mA}\) has \(r_o = 300\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\).

Going the other way, suppose a curve passes through 1.00 mA at 1 V and 1.05 mA at 6 V. Its slope is \(0.01\ \mathrm{mA/V}\), and extrapolating backward it reaches zero at \(1 - 100 = -99\ \mathrm{V}\), so \(V_A \approx 99\ \mathrm{V}\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Placing the intercept at \(+V_A\) instead of \(-V_A\).
- Treating \(r_o\) as fixed. It scales as \(1/I_C\).
- Computing the slope from two points that are not both in forward-active.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: \(r_o\) enters the BJT small-signal model, where it sets the intrinsic gain \(g_mr_o = V_A/V_{th}\). It also limits the output resistance of current mirrors.
